lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Confirmed the forecast gain over the nested HAR-RV baseline with standard Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices.
- Joining 120 microstructure features point-in-time across six venues, deduplicating late prints and versioning each schema, built a feature store the team reused in two later projects.
- Annualized the signal's daily Sharpe ratio by multiplying it by 252 before reporting it to the desk.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.

- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation while maintaining the lab's shared cluster, organizing the weekly reading group and grading for two courses, which was downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Cut forecast error from 0.20 to 0.15, a 33% improvement, by adding realized-volatility features and an asymmetric loss.
- Improved the model's directional hit rate by 6% on 30 equity indices, from 52% to 58%, with a temporal convolutional model.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The résumé opens with Sunrise Bakery instead of the quantitative research and project work most relevant to the target reader.
items.because: A recruiter may initially read the candidate as a store manager, while the strongest evidence of technical fit is pushed below an unrelated role.

items.says: “Managed” does not specify the opening responsibility owned.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the work involved scheduling, opening controls, cash reconciliation, or production coordination.

items.says: The current role uses inconsistent past-tense wording.
items.because: “Managed” and “keeping” make work in a role listed as Present appear dated.

items.says: The labour-budget claim states compliance without the measured result against the approved budget.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the store was barely within budget or materially under it.

items.says: The line attributes the entire decrease in unsold bread to stock counts and supplier orders without establishing that causal effect.
items.because: Demand, promotions, product mix, or production changes could also explain the fall from 12% to 7%.

items.says: “Ran” and “cutting” use past-tense wording for a current role.
items.because: The role is listed as Present.

items.says: The signal description does not identify the specific feature or modeling choice that demonstrates the technical contribution.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the contribution involved imbalance horizons, normalization, forecasting, or portfolio construction.

items.says: “Cost-aware position smoother” does not show how the tool produced the trade-off.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish a meaningful optimization or control method from a generic smoothing adjustment.

items.says: The turnover, retained-return, and slippage results are chained together and difficult to scan.
items.because: The reader must parse several metrics before understanding the smoother’s overall benefit.

items.says: Standard Diebold–Mariano tests are methodologically invalid for confirming a gain in this nested comparison.
items.because: The usual Diebold–Mariano test is not valid without adjustment when an augmented model is compared with a nested HAR-RV model.

items.says: The line does not address dependence or multiple comparisons across the 30 indices.
items.because: Those issues must be addressed before the tests can establish the claimed confirmation.

items.says: The bullet does not state the forecast metric.
items.because: The reader cannot judge what kind of improvement was tested.

items.says: The bullet does not state the size of the forecast gain.
items.because: The reader cannot judge whether the improvement was economically meaningful.

items.says: The bullet names the test without giving a concise test outcome.
items.because: The test name establishes process, not evidence of statistical significance.

items.says: The feature-store bullet begins with a dangling modifier.
items.because: “Joining” does not attach cleanly to the later subject, making the sentence grammatically unstable.

items.says: The feature-store outcome is delayed behind three implementation details.
items.because: The team’s reuse of the feature store is buried and harder to scan for impact.

items.says: The reuse count does not show what the later projects gained from the feature store.
items.because: The number of projects shows reach without showing reduced research time, data errors, or backtesting inconsistency.

items.says: The daily Sharpe ratio was annualized with the wrong formula by multiplying it by 252.
items.because: A daily Sharpe ratio is conventionally annualized by multiplying it by √252, not 252.

items.says: The bullet ends with an administrative reporting action instead of a research or decision outcome.
items.because: Reporting a corrected metric does not show that the work changed a model choice, desk comparison, or investment decision.

items.says: The documentation bullet does not quantify its operational onboarding benefit.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether onboarding time fell, how many interns used the material, or how much friction it removed.

items.says: The relative clause beginning with “which” is ambiguous and indirect.
items.because: “Which” can refer to the wiki or its contents, and “used to onboard” does not directly describe what the documentation did.

items.says: The reproducibility claim overstates what a seed and configuration file can establish on a shared cluster.
items.because: They do not capture code, data, dependencies, software versions, RNG behavior, hardware, or parallel-execution behavior.

items.says: The proof bullet uses the first-person pronoun “my.”
items.because: “My proof” breaks the résumé’s phrase-based style.

items.says: “Previous bound” does not identify the baseline theorem or result.
items.because: A theoretical reader cannot quickly judge the log-factor improvement without knowing which prior bound it improves.

items.says: The teaching bullet does not state what changed for students.
items.because: The rating shows perceived effectiveness, but the reader must infer the educational outcome.

items.says: The package bullet does not identify what the candidate implemented inside the R package.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish developing an estimator or algorithm from packaging existing work.

items.says: The bullet bundles cluster maintenance, reading-group organization, and grading into the package achievement.
items.because: These unrelated duties interrupt the main accomplishment and leave the entry as an unordered task list.

items.says: The download result has an unclear antecedent.
items.because: “Which” can grammatically refer to several preceding activities rather than clearly to the package.

items.says: The claimed “33% improvement” is numerically incorrect.
items.because: Reducing error from 0.20 to 0.15 is a 0.05 absolute reduction or a 25% relative reduction.

items.says: The bullet does not identify the forecast-error metric.
items.because: The values cannot be interpreted without knowing whether the measure is RMSE, MAE, QLIKE, or another metric.

items.says: The bullet repeats the first bullet’s realized-volatility feature method and overlaps with its model-performance result.
items.because: The reader may not know whether the bullets describe separate experiments or duplicate evidence.

items.says: The increase from 52% to 58% is 6 percentage points, not a 6% improvement.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 11.5%.

items.says: The repeated temporal-convolutional-model reference does not explain the distinct contribution.
items.because: It makes the bullet look redundant with the preceding model description.

items.says: The 0.02 validation-to-leaderboard gap does not identify its metric or units.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether 0.02 is an absolute score difference, a percentage, or another measure.

items.says: “Closed” does not show which score moved.
items.because: Without the direction of movement, the effect of changing the folds is difficult to judge.

items.says: The bullet does not state the resulting validation-to-leaderboard gap.
items.because: Without the final gap, the effect of changing the folds is difficult to judge.

items.says: “Without losing validation score” does not identify the validation metric.
items.because: The result cannot be independently judged without naming the score being preserved.

items.says: The bullet does not show how closely the reduced-feature model matched the original.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the score was exactly preserved, approximately preserved, or within a stated tolerance.

items.says: The Methods line misspells “econometrics” as “econometircs.”
items.because: The visible misspelling weakens the credibility of a directly relevant technical skill.

items.says: Kafka is listed under Programming without evidence of its use elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: The reader may question whether Kafka was actually used, particularly because it is not connected to the feature-store work.
